active_paradigms.idea: Joint 26-variable Sequential Linear Programming (SLP) trust-region refinement: move all 13 points simultaneously via scipy.optimize.linprog
active_paradigms.description: The current one-point LP finds the exact best move for a single point, which means the incumbent is only optimal with respect to single-point perturbations; the remaining gap to the benchmark almost certainly requires coordinated motion of several points at once. Formulate a joint LP over 27 variables: the 26 coordinate displacements of all points plus the bottleneck value t. Around the incumbent p (affinely renormalized so hull area = 1, which the ratio permits), fix orientation signs s_ijk = sign(D_ijk(p)) for all 286 triples and use the exact first-order expansion of each signed area D_ijk(p + delta) = D_ijk(p) + grad(D_ijk)·delta, whose entries are simple edge terms like (y_j - y_k) and (x_k - x_j). Maximize t subject to s_ijk·(D_ijk(p) + grad·delta) >= 2t for all triples, a linearized hull-area constraint H(p) + grad(H)·delta <= 1 (shoelace gradient over current hull vertices only, interior points have zero gradient), and an L-infinity trust region |delta| <= delta encoded directly as linprog variable bounds. After each solve, recompute the exact true ratio (all 286 areas plus exact hull area via the existing monotone chain) and accept only strict improvements; adapt delta by the actual-to-predicted improvement ratio (expand x2 above 0.75, shrink x0.5 below 0.25, reject and shrink on degradation), re-deriving signs and the hull vertex set after every accepted step. Iterate down to delta ~ 1e-6, then interleave with the existing perturbation-restart loop so every restart basin gets polished by joint moves, not one-point moves. This directly escapes the single-point-local-optimum trap where, for example, two adjacent hull vertices must slide together while interior points shift to compensate.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary): escape single-point-move local optima by computing exact coordinated multi-point ascent directions; combined_score from 0.9775 toward > 1.0. eval_time secondary: each LP has only 27 variables and ~287 constraints, solving in milliseconds, so thousands of SLP iterations fit in the budget.
active_paradigms.cautions: Orientation signs must be re-derived after every accepted step, and any step where a triangle's signed area crosses zero without being modeled must be rejected via the true-ratio test. The linearized hull-area constraint is only valid while the hull vertex set is unchanged; cap the initial trust region at delta=0.1 and rely on exact acceptance to guard hull-set changes. Renormalize the configuration (affine rescale) so hull area is 1 after each accepted step to keep the linearization numerically stable. Handle linprog failures by halving delta rather than aborting, and keep HiGHS calls deterministic. Budget roughly 120s for SLP phases inside the existing 280s deadline, always falling back to the incumbent on failure.

active_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-reduced exhaustive global structure search: quasi-random Sobol sampling of 4-12 parameter configuration families, then symmetry-breaking polish
active_paradigms.description: Random 26-dimensional restarts explore configuration structure only by luck; instead, parameterize highly structured candidate families with very few parameters and sample them quasi-exhaustively. Family A (C3 rotational symmetry, 8 parameters): center plus 4 orbits of 3 points at radii r_m and angles theta_m + 2*pi*k/3; Family B (C6 symmetry, 4 parameters): center plus two hexagonal orbits; Family C (reflection symmetry, 12 parameters): one point on the axis plus 6 mirrored pairs (x_m, +/-y_m). Generate 2^15 scrambled Sobol points per family with scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol(d, scramble=True, seed=fixed_seed), mapping radii log-uniformly into [0.05, 1.5] and angles uniformly, then evaluate the exact ratio for every candidate with a fully vectorized batched determinant computation over the 286 index triples (chunked einsum, a few seconds for ~10^5 configurations). Keep the top ~300 candidates per family, refine each within its reduced parameter space using scipy.optimize.minimize with method='Nelder-Mead' (deterministic, derivative-free, cheap in at most 12 dimensions, maxiter around 2000), then deliberately break symmetry by adding small fixed-seed Gaussian perturbations to the full 26 coordinates and polishing with the existing coordinate-descent plus one-point LP machinery. This determines the globally best structural pattern (ring nest versus double hexagon versus mirrored layout, and the optimal radii/angles within it) rather than hoping a random walk lands in the right basin; additionally, project the current 0.9775 incumbent onto each family (least-squares fit of radii/angles) to seed extra local refinements. The low dimensionality is what makes true global coverage possible where 26-dimensional restarts cannot achieve it.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary): discover a fundamentally better structural basin (ring radii, angular offsets, hull cardinality pattern) that 26-dim random restarts miss; combined_score toward > 1.0. eval_time secondary: batch evaluation is fully vectorized and total sampling plus refinement fits in 60-90 seconds.
active_paradigms.cautions: Exact symmetry creates structural degeneracies: two orbits sharing the same angle put three points on one ray through the center (zero-area triangle), so many samples score near 0 - this is fine since they are simply discarded, but refinement must not start from near-degenerate samples (filter by a minimum ratio threshold before Nelder-Mead). The true optimum may break symmetry entirely, so the symmetry-breaking perturbation and full-dimensional polish stage is essential, not optional. Vectorize batch evaluation in chunks of ~2048 configurations to keep memory bounded, and fix the Sobol seed and refinement order for reproducibility. Do not spend refinement time on families whose best sampled ratio is far below the incumbent; allocate the ~60-90s budget proportionally to each family's best sampled value.

active_paradigms.idea: Smooth-min (log-sum-exp) homotopy with analytic gradients over all 26 coordinates via scipy.optimize.minimize L-BFGS-B
active_paradigms.description: The true objective is a non-smooth minimum of 286 triangle areas divided by the hull area; replace it with the smooth softmin m_beta(p) = -(1/beta)·log(sum_i exp(-beta·s_i(p))) where s_i = 30·A_i/H are scale-normalized triangle areas, and maximize it with L-BFGS-B using exact analytic gradients (the problem needs no constraints at all because the evaluator imposes no container and the ratio is affine-invariant). Supply fun and jac together to scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B'): the softmin gradient with respect to each s_i is the softmax weight w_i; the partial derivatives of each triangle area with respect to its three vertices are signed edge terms like +/-(y_j - y_k)/2 using the current orientation sign; and the hull-area gradient is nonzero only on hull vertices (shoelace derivative), combined via the quotient rule for A_i/H, with the hull vertex set recomputed each evaluation by a 13-point monotone chain costing microseconds. Run a continuation (homotopy) schedule beta = 10 up to 3e4 in about 15 geometric steps, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution: early small-beta stages weight many triangles at once and therefore move points in coordinated groups, while late large-beta stages sharpen to the exact bottleneck - this automatically produces the multi-point coordinated moves that greedy coordinate descent cannot. Multistart from about 100 deterministic starts (regular 13-gon, 3-fold nest, double hexagon, the current incumbent, and scrambled Sobol clouds in 26 dims), keep the global best, and polish the winner with the existing one-point LP refinement for final exactness. Each full homotopy chain costs well under a second (hundreds of iterations times O(286) vectorized flops), so hundreds of starts fit comfortably alongside the existing search phases.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary): gradient-driven coordinated repositioning of all points with a smooth-min surrogate that anneals from group motion to exact bottleneck maximization; combined_score toward > 1.0. eval_time secondary: vectorized objective plus analytic Jacobian makes each homotopy run sub-second, allowing hundreds of deterministic multistarts within the time budget.
active_paradigms.cautions: Scale the normalized areas by a factor (~30) so they are O(1) before applying beta, and implement log-sum-exp with max-subtraction to avoid overflow at large beta. Starting beta too large collapses the gradient onto a single triangle (subgradient-like stalling), so the continuation schedule from soft to sharp is essential. The hull area H appears in a denominator: guard against numerical blow-up when the configuration shrinks by affinely renormalizing to hull area 1 every few hundred iterations, and treat H as piecewise-smooth (gradient defined only on hull vertices; kinks when the hull set changes are rare and tolerated by L-BFGS-B). Refresh orientation signs for the |D|/2 area gradients at every evaluation to handle orientation flips, verify jac numerically against finite differences once during development, and keep everything deterministic (fixed seeds, deterministic optimizer) for reproducibility.

tried_paradigms.idea: Smooth surrogate optimization with annealed LogSumExEx soft-min via scipy.optimize.minimize
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the non-smooth greedy coordinate descent with a proper gradient-based local optimizer on a smooth surrogate: r_soft = -temperature * logsumexp(-areas/temperature) / hull_area, where hull_area is also smoothed via a log-sum-exp over convex hull support directions (or held fixed once the hull vertex set stabilizes). Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' or 'L-BFGS-B' on all 26 coordinates, starting from the current best configuration and from symmetric seeds. Anneal the temperature from ~1e-2 down to ~1e-5 over successive minimize calls, warm-starting each stage. Analytic or finite-difference gradients both work since only 26 variables exist. This escapes the axis-aligned step-size limitations of the current coordinate descent, which can only move along 8 fixed directions and plateaus on the ratio objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary): smooth optimization can find exact local optima of the true objective that greedy 8-direction coordinate descent cannot reach, pushing combined_score above 1.0.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Soft-min temperature must be annealed carefully; too cold makes gradients vanish. Keep the hull area term smooth by using a fixed hull or log-sum-exp over hull edge contributions. Guard against degenerate hulls (area < 1e-9) with a large penalty.

tried_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-restricted parametric families with exhaustive low-dimensional search
tried_paradigms.description: Restrict the search to configurations with exact 3-fold rotational symmetry: 13 = 1 + 4*3, i.e., a center point plus 4 orbits of 3 points each, parameterized by only ~9 free parameters (4 radii, 4 angles, plus center offset). Exhaustively grid-search this low-dimensional parameter space (radii in [0.05, 1.0], angles in [0, 2pi/3)) at coarse resolution, then refine the top candidates with the existing local search but allowing symmetry-breaking perturbations. Also try 13 = 1 + 6 + 6 (center + two hexagon orbits, 13 free params), and 13 = 3 + 5 + 5 style nests. The massive dimensionality reduction (9-13 params vs 26) means a near-exhaustive coverage of the symmetric subspace is feasible within the 240s budget, potentially finding structured optima that random restarts miss. Keep the best-of-all-families result and compare against the unconstrained incumbent.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized: structured families concentrate search effort on geometrically balanced configurations where the min-triangle bottleneck is naturally large.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The optimal 13-point configuration likely has NO perfect symmetry (13 is prime, and known good Heilbronn configs are often asymmetric), so always run the unconstrained refinement as a final polish and comparison. Ensure determinism with fixed seeds and fixed grid ordering.

tried_paradigms.idea: Bottleneck-guided LP moves: maximize the minimum triangle via linear programming on active constraints
tried_paradigms.description: Formulate each local improvement step as a linear program: given the current configuration, the area of triangle (i,j,k) is an affine function of any single moved point p_i (area = 0.5*|cross(p_j - p_i, p_k - p_i)|; for fixed j,k and small moves the sign of the cross product is stable, making it linear). Solve max t subject to: for every triangle containing point i, linearized_area >= t, plus a trust region ||p_i - p_i^0|| <= delta, using scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS). Iterate over points i (or move all points with a joint LP using sequential linearization of all 286 area constraints), shrinking the trust region as convergence approaches. This directly optimizes the true max-min objective (not a surrogate) with exact global steps within each trust region, unlike coordinate descent which only tests 8 directions per point per step size. Alternate with occasional hull-area reduction moves (pulling interior hull vertices inward) since the ratio also improves by shrinking the hull.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized: LP steps provably find the best single-point move within the trust region, eliminating direction/step-size discretization error entirely.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The min-area constraint set may be empty for aggressive t; use bisection on t with feasibility checks. The hull area changes as points move, so re-linearize every few iterations and only accept steps that strictly improve the true ratio. Handle degenerate triangles (zero gradient) by dropping those constraints and relying on the true-objective check.
